text: /// Record consent decisions: approvals into `[plugins] auto-enable`,
/// declines into `[plugins] disable`, then save the config. Both lists hold
/// dependency crate names, as [`discover`] offers them.
/// Split out from the prompt so the decision recording is testable without a
/// terminal, and so other entry points can record the same way.
pub fn apply_consent(sym: &mut Symposium, approved: &[String], declined: &[String]) -> Result<()> {

rationale:
`apply_consent`, after `save_config()` succeeds, emits a `ReportEvent::Info` at info level "enabled dependency plugins: <names>" when any were approved, and "declined dependency plugins (recorded in `[plugins] disable`): <names>" when any were declined. The report layer renders `Info` events to stdout in normal mode (`--json` collects them), so the user sees both lists. Nothing is printed when both lists are empty (early return).

Untested: no test asserts these messages (`apply_consent_records_both_answers` checks only the config); judged from code. A test using the `with_report` helper in `tests/enablement.rs` would cover it.
requirement: After recording consent answers, Symposium SHOULD tell the user which dependency plugins it enabled and which it declined.
